model.authority: one assumed external linearizer supplies the operation order
model.outcome: one outcome per input operation plus the final reduced state
model.client_labels: opaque illustrative strings, not identities or product claims

limit_semantics.labels: the UTF-8 byte limit applies to every ID, actor label, object ID, and field key
limit_semantics.collections: field, note, operation, array, and object-member maxima are inclusive
limit_semantics.depth: at most 63 nested JSON containers around a scalar are accepted; 64 reject

operation_precedence: an exact duplicate operation ID and canonical operation is idempotent
a reused operation ID with different canonical content is OPERATION_ID_CONFLICT
otherwise a final object rejects with OBJECT_FINAL
otherwise a mismatched expected revision rejects with STALE_REVISION
otherwise operation-specific no-change or conflict checks apply
otherwise the operation applies and increments revision exactly once
invariants: the caller-supplied operation list is the only ordering authority
rejected and idempotent outcomes never mutate state or advance revision
every applied operation advances revision by exactly one
the final revision equals initial revision plus applied outcome count
final object mutability status is sticky; it is not task, attempt, agent, or fleet lifecycle state
operation ID conflict is checked before finality and revision
field and note equality uses exact Unicode scalar and canonical JSON semantics with no normalization
same canonical input produces byte-identical JavaScript and Python output
non_claims: no unordered merge, CRDT, OT, vector clock, Lamport clock, causality graph, or clock behavior
no envelope, transport, delivery, batching, receipt, acknowledgment, routing, ranking, provider, model, or adapter behavior
no task, attempt, agent, fleet, cancellation, settlement, recovery, or other lifecycle behavior
no lease, partition, quorum, policy, authorization, identity proof, authentication, signature, trust, or attestation
no persistence, datastore, filesystem artifact access, URI, content transfer, runtime execution, tool invocation, or side effect
no named-client capability or production interoperability claim
no merge, push, publication, deployment, activation, or release authority
